OpenMuse Introduces Personal Agent Framework with Browser and Terminal Integration

04 Nov 2026, 06:32 AM IST · GlobeWire Daily Editorial Desk · Source: github.com

1 min read

Key takeaways

Image: GitHub · Photo source · Resized and letterboxed to 16:9; no AI generation

In this article
  1. Overview
  2. Core Capabilities
  3. Deployment and Configuration
  4. Verification and Resources

Overview

OpenMuse is an open-source personal agent application built with CopilotKit and AG-UI, designed to handle ongoing tasks across a browser, terminal, file system, and mobile or web interfaces. The application supports local testing without external model configurations and provides deployment blueprints for platforms like Render.

Core Capabilities

  • Multi-Environment Support: Runs natively on iOS, Android, and web via React Native.
  • Agent Computer Integration: Combines persistent Chromium browsing with an optional Linux workspace for executing terminal commands and managing PDFs.
  • Task and Goal Tracking: Features built-in workflows for goal tracking, delegated tasks, and simulated local interactions such as drafting form responses and managing mock availability checks.

Deployment and Configuration

Deploying OpenMuse involves setting up environment variables, database requirements, and optional workers:

  • Server Requirements: Requires Node 24 LTS, pnpm 11.19.0, and a CopilotKit Intelligence project key.
  • Cloud Deployment: Configuration files are provided for deploying services including the API, web app, and private browser worker.
  • Security and Storage: Uses encrypted credentials at rest and local storage directories for PGlite databases, documents, and signing keys.

Verification and Resources

Users can inspect the source code under the MIT license, review documentation, and test local workflows using documented setup steps and mock demos.
